R0003.title: Malicious Flash Sale Grabbing
R0003.definition: Using automated means to grab goods or services during flash sales.
R0003.description: Also known as malicious order snatching. Refers to bad actors using technical means such as purchase-grabbing software to maliciously snatch time-limited, limited-quantity discounted goods on e-commerce platforms, disrupting normal market order and consumer shopping experience. These tools simulate human operations such as login, clicking, and order submission to achieve automated purchasing.
R0003.influence: Exploits platform promotional benefits, disrupts normal platform operations, and degrades the ordering and shopping experience for legitimate users.

references.title: Four convicted for making and selling Lalamove plug-ins; over 20,000 drivers reportedly banned for plug-in use...

observables: Order-submission QPS for limited-stock items spikes instantly at the drop, far exceeding normal levels
Order requests align precisely with inventory release timing, with millisecond-level response
The same shipping address or payment account is tied to rush-buy orders from many different accounts

R0003-001.title: Instant Bid Sniping
R0003-001.definition: Placing a bid at the first possible moment to obtain limited or flash-sale goods or services through unfair means.
R0003-001.description: Using unfair methods to obtain limited or flash-sale goods, services, or discounts — typically via third-party scripts or auxiliary tools. Sometimes relies on third-party intelligence to pre-leak interface information. Usually requires process automation capabilities (R0001).
R0003-001.influence: Exploits platform promotional benefits and disrupts legitimate user ordering.

observables: Bidding-endpoint QPS spikes instantly at the activity start and concentrates within a millisecond window
Request arrival time shows minimal deviation from the activity start time, exhibiting batch-script characteristics
A single account completes the full coupon-claim to order to payment chain within an extremely short window, with no browsing dwell time
Bidding requests from multiple accounts show highly clustered device fingerprints or IP ranges

R0003-002.title: Auction Sniping
R0003-002.definition: Placing a bid on goods or services in the final minute of an auction to win at a low price.
R0003-002.description: Using automated means to place a bid at the last minute, often completing a transaction at minimal cost. The principle is the same as instant bid sniping (R0003) but the goal differs: auction sniping aims to be the last valid bid before the deadline to obtain goods at the lowest possible price, while instant bid sniping aims to be the first bid after the sale starts to secure limited discounted items. Auction sniping typically requires process automation (R0001).
R0003-002.influence: Transaction prices are too low, resulting in insufficient profit margins. Disrupts legitimate user ordering.

observables: Bidding requests concentrate in the final seconds before auction close, exhibiting batch-concurrent characteristics
Bid timestamps show highly consistent intervals from the auction end time, with multiple accounts acting in sync
Winning bid prices are far below the items' market value, with abnormally low closing prices
The same device/IP triggers synchronized last-second bids across multiple auctions ending near the same time

R0003-003.title: Bot Scalping Risk
R0003-003.definition: Bots refer to the practice of seizing, misappropriating, or manipulating scarce resources through illegitimate means, especially using automated crawler techniques.
R0003-003.description: Using automated scripts or crawler tools to register large numbers of fake accounts, simulating transaction activity and fictitious purchases to seize scarce resources on the platform — such as limited-edition goods or purchase eligibility — preventing legitimate users from having a fair chance.
R0003-003.influence: Scarce resources are seized by fake accounts, preventing legitimate users from obtaining purchase opportunities; platform marketing inventory and activity eligibility are consumed, while fake transaction data distorts ranking and reputation.

references.title: Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Transactions

observables: Limited-stock items are swept by newly registered accounts at the drop instant, with account registration times highly clustered
Ordering accounts show batch-homogenized shipping addresses, payment methods, and contact information
Scalping accounts lack normal browsing, cart-add, and comparison steps in their behavioral trail before and after transactions
The same device fingerprint or IP is tied to large numbers of fake accounts repeatedly seizing scarce resources

R0003-004.title: Unfair Resource Seizure
R0003-004.definition: Unfair resource seizure risk refers to individuals or organizations using illegitimate means to compete for and seize limited resources, violating fair competition principles and potentially causing unfair resource distribution and system abuse.
R0003-004.description: Specific illegitimate means include but are not limited to: using bot programs to rapidly submit large numbers of requests the moment resources become available; using malicious software to attack target systems; exploiting system vulnerabilities to bypass normal allocation mechanisms; submitting false personal or application information to deceive the system.
R0003-004.influence: May lead to unfair resource distribution, system overload, and escalating malicious competition.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT-021 Denial of Inventory

observables: Submission volume for registration, enrollment, or ticket-grabbing endpoints spikes the instant resources are released and concentrates within a millisecond window
Submitted personal-information fields show batch-generation patterns, such as consecutive ID-card numbers or mobile-number ranges
Seizure requests originate from highly clustered IPs and device fingerprints, with multiple accounts triggering in sync
Accounts that successfully seize resources exhibit resale or transfer behavior shortly after obtaining them
